circuitpython_stdout_note: CircuitPython 11.0.0-alpha.2's own answer, at the same ceiling this port ships (64). ALL EIGHT LINES are identical to `stdout` and to desktop MicroPython. Until 2026-09-09 three differed, and this note blamed the deliberate biquad deviations for all three; that was wrong on every count. Each had its own cause, and all four are fixed: (1) `lead` -- the biquad deviation was applied on ONE TARGET ONLY (audiodsp#77); synthio.Biquad now runs CircuitPython's Q15 on every target. (2) `bend` -- the zero-crossing loudness gate read the wrong voice slot on the CPython twin, whose note list compacts where CircuitPython's channel array does not; each note now carries the channel it was admitted on. (3) part of the SAW waveform -- the test-only ulab bridge rounded where real ulab truncates (tests/support/ulab). (4) `bass` -- the twin rendered voices already at envelope level 0, which the native builds skip. Harmless until the gate existed, because pending loudness 0 contributes silence; with the gate the voice kept sounding at its previous loudness for a whole block (audiodsp#78). Pinned by tests/test_cpython_silenced_voice.py, whose three cases all fail with the skip removed. Re-captured for audiodsp's resync with 11.0.0-alpha.2: upstream's mixer now scales a voice in integers, `(x * level) >> 15`, so `lead`, `bend` and `bass` moved, and the oracle, this port and desktop MicroPython agree on all eight lines again.
